name: Biao-Jiao Mien
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Goedemans, Rob & Harry van der Hulst. 2010. Word accent systems in the languages of Asia. In van der Hulst, Goedemans & van Zanten (eds.), A survey of word accentual patterns in the languages of the world, ch.10, pp.509-599. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
sources.note: Lists Biao-Jiao Mien in the Hmong-Mien classification but under 'Accent information' (p.596) says only: 'Hmong-Mien is usually described as being exclusively tonal... Unfortunately, we did not have access to sources that would allow us to elaborate on this point.' No language-specific statement.

sources.citation: Solnit, David B. 1985. Introduction to the Biao Min Yao language. Cahiers de Linguistique Asie Orientale 14(2): 175-191. DOI 10.3406/clao.1985.1175 (Persée).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing. Section 2 'Phonology' (pp.178-183) gives syllable canon (C)(M)V(Co)+tone, initials, medials, rhymes and six tones (1=44, 2=21 breathy, 3=35, 4=42 short glottalised, 5=24, 7=54 short glottalised); section 3 describes tone (and consonant) sandhi in which all non-final syllables of the 'nominal nucleus' of an NP take a sandhi tone. The words stress/accent do not occur; no statement about word stress or its absence.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2017. Biao Min (Guanyang). MSEA Languages web page (field notes; audio word lists Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.1123261, 10.5281/zenodo.1123263), Wayback capture 2020-10-09.
sources.note: Dialect classification and a few sound correspondences only; nothing on stress.
